title: fix(flow): unblock captures and simplify review navigation
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix capture queues blocking later screens: Screens and Map capture only the selected situation, stop polling completed or failed captures, and provide an explicit retry.
- Add `/screens`, `/map`, and `/journey` routes; default to Screens and preserve the selected route through reviewer login.
- Allow entering Journey before fixture preparation, applying the selected situation on entry. Add capture failure diagnostics without exposing OAuth URLs.
- Validated locally: 261 tests passed; production build, typecheck and Biome passed; native Linux containers passed real journeys, captures, two-reviewer isolation, restart and replacement at 0.5 CPU / 4 GiB. Exact Linux/amd64 container verification remains required in CI before merge.

gist.headline: One screen at a time
gist.blurb: Flow reviews no longer wait on a capture that has already finished—or failed. Reviewers can retry a capture and move between Screens, Map, and Journey without losing their place.
gist.summary: Flow now captures only the selected situation, stops polling finished or failed captures, offers an explicit retry, and adds /screens, /map, and /journey routes that survive reviewer login.
gist.impact: Reviewers can continue past a failed capture, open Journey before fixture preparation, and return from login to their selected review view.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Flow as a cozy review desk with three clearly marked paths—Screens, Map, and Journey. Polli guides a CRT monitor robot from a stalled picture frame to a fresh capture, with a small retry button, a route signpost, and code-plants nearby.
